source.title: Jazz Piano Voicings — Transcribed Comping from Volume 60 Freddie Hubbard

pieces.title: Little Sunflower
transcription_observed: sustained sonorities alternate with short chord attacks
rests remain part of the texture
repeated rhythmic cells occur without becoming the only realization
later excerpt shows denser block-like activity and thicker texture
register and voicing size change within recurring harmony

design_inference.key_hypothesis: static harmony can support changing accompaniment narrative

pieces.title: Gibraltar
transcription_observed: recognizable recurring rhythmic placements across harmonic cycles
pattern identity persists while exact realization varies
later sections alternate sparse attacks, held sonorities, repeated short cells and denser blocks
rests continue to appear inside active comping

design_inference.key_hypothesis: pattern consistency and variation pressure must be independent controls

pieces.title: Crisis
transcription_observed: sustained support alternates with short punctuation and rests
compact and wider sonorities both appear
linear/chromatic motion appears between harmonic events
texture changes around formal and harmonic boundaries

design_inference.key_hypothesis: continuity policy should depend on harmonic/form context

cross_piece_hypotheses.statement: same harmony can support multiple piano actions
repetition may function as groove/form identity rather than mechanical redundancy
variation pressure and pattern consistency should be independently represented
harmonic stability/rate of change should influence continuity policy

cautions: No literal phrase or voicing sequence should be memorized as a future template.
Qualitative labels are not exact statistical measurements.
Audio and expert review are needed before calibrating numeric weights.
